name: crandel
author: clothes-dressing-packing designer
description: Washing hanging on a drying rack, drawn small. THE CLUE IS THE EMPTY RACK: rail rows of "=" with the pegs "v" already placed (two pegs per garment: they mark where that garment's left and right edge will be), the air rows between the rails drawn as dots, and ONE NUMBER per rail written two spaces after the right-hand end of that rail row. 2-3 rails (3 in 86% of clues), 3-4 garments per rail, racks 18-24 columns wide, 2-4 air rows under each rail. THE ANSWER IS THE CLUE'S PICTURE WITH THE WASHING HUNG ON IT: each garment is a block of one capital letter filling the columns between its two pegs, hanging from the top air row of its rail downwards; the only free choice is HOW FAR DOWN each garment hangs (1 row .. all the way to the rail below). THE RULE, one clause: the number on a rail is how many of its garments hang ALL THE WAY DOWN to the rail below AND hang over the daylight BETWEEN TWO GARMENTS down there - the water goes past the washing and drips on the floor between two things. The bottom rail has nothing below it, so its number is always 0. SCORER: it rebuilds the clue from the picture (pegs at the two ends of every garment in the top air row of each block, one dot row per air row, and the drip count per rail) and compares strings, so the rack, its width, its row counts and its peg positions are all forced to match and only the hems are free. PRIVATE - DISCOVERY PATH: the clue alone says "hang the washing from these pegs" (garrow's whole pizza, fennick's empty shelf), so a demo-less player sends a well-formed rack and scores from the foothold - "N of them reach the line below" pays 21.0%, "hang everything all the way down" 21.1%, random hems 13.1%. The demo is what buys the rule: every shipped demo shows, on the top rail, a counted garment dripping through a gap NEXT TO a long garment that lands squarely on a garment below (not counted), and a short garment (not counted); 55% of demos also show a short garment that IS over a gap (length matters) and 32% a long garment poking past the END of the rail below (floor, but no gap: not counted). WITNESS TABLE (700 fresh clues, every attacker knows the grammar and hangs its garments from the right pegs, differing only in which garments it decides to hang all the way down): true rule 100%; "bare floor under part of it" 32.6%; "not sitting squarely on one garment" 32.3%; every garment full length 21.1%; "N of them reach the line below" 21.0%; "overlaps something below" (the v2 rule) 16.7%; random hems 13.1%; "fully covers something below" 7.3%; leftmost N hang full (aligned columns) 5.1%; "lands on two or more garments" 3.6%; one fixed answer for every clue 0.1%; clue echoed / every garment one row / demo replayed / junk 0.0%. So the no-insight ceiling is ~21% and the nearest wrong law pays ~33%: nothing above 50%, and clues do not repeat (20000 distinct in 20000 seeds), so there is nothing to cache. HYPOTHESIS ELIMINATION over 16 readings of the same picture, ONE demo (500 demos, % killed): "hangs all the way down" 100%, "every garment" 100%, "lands on two or more" 99.8%, "straddles the whole gap" 99.8%, "over a gap and touching nothing" 98.8%, "nothing at all under it" 95.4%, "lands on something below" 94.2%, "completely covers something" 93.2%, "lands on exactly one" 93.2%, "3 or more wide" 85.2%, "bare floor under part of it" 83.4%, "not sitting squarely on one garment" 83.4%, "the ones that stop short" 80.2%, "over a gap however long it is" 79.6%, "over a gap 2+ wide" 77.6%. So one demo leaves ~2 live rivals out of 16 and the survivors are all one probing round away. v4 (2026-09-05, demo-economy rebuild for the 7-class / 4-round / 3-demo format, after both players scored 0% on v3 in lad-crandel-v3-1 and reported that "331/231/3" said nothing about the shape of an answer): the object moved into the clue and the digits moved onto the rails; "rows" and "longs" are gone from the clue (the rails and pegs carry the widths, the air rows carry the gaps), leaving one number per rail; garment positions and widths are pinned by the pegs so the whole answer is a length decision per garment. Every rail is built to hold at least one gap-hanger and at least one end-poker, the top rail also a squarely-lander, and the number runs 1..(gap-hangers), so no rail's number can be read off the picture without the rule. Author: clothes/dressing/packing direction.

# an empty drying rack: rail rows with pegs, empty air rows, one number per rail.
# Kinds of garment, relative to the rail below:
#   C hangs over the daylight between two garments below (the counted one)
#   S sits squarely inside one garment below      E pokes past the end (floor, but no gap)
# Every rail carries at least one C and at least one E, the top rail also an S, and the
# number runs 1..(number of Cs), so no rail's number can be read off without the rule.
def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)

    def lay(k, W, pad):  # k garments, widths 2-5, >=1 apart, margin pad at both ends
        slack = W - 2 * pad - (k - 1) - 2 * k
        if slack < 0: return None
        w = [2] * k
        for _ in range(r.randint(0, min(slack, 3 * k))):
            i = r.randrange(k)
            if w[i] < 5: w[i] += 1; slack -= 1
        c = sorted(r.randint(0, slack) for _ in range(k))
        x, out = pad, []
        for i in range(k):
            x += c[i] - (c[i - 1] if i else 0)
            out += [(x, x + w[i])]
            x += w[i] + 1
        return out

    def shelf(A, W, pool, pad):  # a rail above A holding one of these mixes of garment
        G = [(a[1], b[0]) for a, b in zip(A, A[1:])]
        O = [o for o in [(0, A[0][0]), (A[-1][1], W)] if o[1] > o[0]]
        c = {"C": [], "S": [], "E": [], "X": [], "N": []}
        for w in range(2, 6):
            for x in range(pad, W - w - pad + 1):
                g = (x, x + w)
                h = [q for q in G if x < q[1] and q[0] < x + w]
                if h:
                    c["C"] += [g]
                    if all(q[1] - q[0] < 2 for q in h): c["N"] += [g]
                elif any(a <= x and x + w <= b for a, b in A): c["S"] += [g]
                elif any(x < q and p < x + w for p, q in O): c["E"] += [g]
                else: c["X"] += [g]
        for _ in range(20):
            need = r.choice(pool)
            if any(not c[t] for t in need): continue
            P = []
            for t in sorted(need, key="ESXC".index):
                q = c["N"] if t == "C" and c["N"] and r.random() < .5 else c[t]
                q = [g for g in q if all(g[1] < u[0] or u[1] < g[0] for u in P)]
                if not q: break
                P += [r.choice(q)]
            if len(P) == len(need): return sorted(P)
        return None

    TOP = [["C", "C", "S", "E"]] * 9 + [["C", "S", "E"]]
    MID = [["C", "C", "E", "E"]] * 4 + [["C", "C", "E"]] * 2 + [["C", "C", "S", "E"]] + [["C", "C", "C", "E"]]
    for _ in range(60):
        W = r.randint(18, 24)
        R = r.choice([2] + [3] * 9)
        rows = [r.choice([2, 2, 3, 3, 4]) for _ in range(R)]
        B = [None] * R
        B[R - 1] = lay(r.choice([3, 3, 4]), W, 2)
        if B[R - 1] is None: continue
        for i in range(R - 2, -1, -1):
            B[i] = shelf(B[i + 1], W, TOP if i == 0 else MID, 1 if i == 0 else 2)
            if B[i] is None: break
        if None in B: continue
        num = []
        for i in range(R - 1):
            G = [(a[1], b[0]) for a, b in zip(B[i + 1], B[i + 1][1:])]
            C = [g for g in B[i] if any(g[0] < q and p < g[1] for p, q in G)]
            cap = min(len(C), len(B[i]) - 2 if i == 0 else len(B[i]) - 1)
            num += [r.randint(1, cap - 1) if cap > 1 and r.random() < .65 else cap]
        num += [0]
        out = []
        for i in range(R):
            q = ["="] * W
            for x, y in B[i]: q[x] = q[y - 1] = "v"
            out += ["".join(q) + "  %d" % num[i]] + ["." * W] * rows[i]
        return "\n".join(out)

# Hang the washing from the pegs: the only choice is how far down each garment hangs.
# The demo shows a counted one beside a long one that lands squarely, a long one past the
# end and a short one, and rejects 15 rival readings of the picture before it ships.
def solve(clue):
    r = random.Random(clue)
    P = []
    for L in clue.split("\n"):
        if "=" in L:
            v = [i for i, ch in enumerate(L) if ch == "v"]
            P += [[L, int(L[-1]), 0, [(v[i], v[i + 1] + 1) for i in range(0, len(v), 2)]]]
        else:
            P[-1][2] += 1
    W = len(P[0][0]) - 3
    R = len(P)
    N = [p[1] for p in P]
    A = [p[3] for p in P]
    ov = lambda u, v: u[0] < v[1] and v[0] < u[1]

    def facts(i):
        if i == R - 1: return [{} for g in A[i]]
        S = A[i + 1]
        G = [(a[1], b[0]) for a, b in zip(S, S[1:])]
        out = []
        for g in A[i]:
            hit = [q for q in G if ov(g, q)]
            on = [q for q in S if ov(g, q)]
            out += [dict(
                c=bool(hit), on=len(on), nil=not on,
                sq=any(q[0] <= g[0] and g[1] <= q[1] for q in S),
                bare=any(all(not (q[0] <= x < q[1]) for q in S) for x in range(*g)),
                cov=any(g[0] <= q[0] and q[1] <= g[1] for q in S),
                wide=g[1] - g[0] > 2, big=any(q[1] - q[0] > 1 for q in hit),
                str8=any(g[0] < q[0] and q[1] < g[1] for q in hit))]
        return out

    F = [facts(i) for i in range(R)]
    RIV = [lambda f, L: L, lambda f, L: L and f["on"], lambda f, L: L and f["bare"],
           lambda f, L: L and not f["sq"], lambda f, L: L and f["on"] > 1,
           lambda f, L: f["c"], lambda f, L: L and f["c"] and f["big"],
           lambda f, L: L and f["nil"], lambda f, L: L and f["cov"],
           lambda f, L: L and f["wide"], lambda f, L: 1, lambda f, L: not L,
           lambda f, L: L and f["c"] and f["str8"], lambda f, L: L and f["on"] == 1,
           lambda f, L: L and f["c"] and not f["big"]]
    WT = [1, 2, 4, 4, 1, 3, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1]

    def hang(i, lg):
        return [P[i][2] if j in lg else r.randint(1, P[i][2] - 1) for j in range(len(A[i]))]

    def draw(H):
        out = []
        pal = r.sample("TSPJDCHV", r.randint(3, 5))
        for i in range(R):
            rows = [["."] * W for _ in range(P[i][2])]
            prev = ""
            for j, (a, b) in enumerate(A[i]):
                ch = r.choice([x for x in pal if x != prev]); prev = ch
                for y in range(H[i][j]):
                    for x in range(a, b): rows[y][x] = ch
            out += [P[i][0]] + ["".join(z) for z in rows]
        return "\n".join(out)

    def chk(s):
        B = []
        for x in s.split("\n"):
            if "=" in x: B += [[]]
            else: B[-1] += [{m.span() for m in re.finditer("[A-Z]+", x)}]
        O = ""
        for b, e in zip(B, B[1:] + [[set()]]):
            q = ["="] * W
            for x, y in b[0]: q[x] = q[y - 1] = "v"
            Z = sorted(e[0])
            n = sum(any(u[0] < y[0] > x[1] < u[1] for x, y in zip(Z, Z[1:]))
                    for u in b[0] & b[-1])
            O += "".join(q) + "  %d\n" % n + ("." * W + "\n") * len(b)
        return O[:-1] == clue

    best = None
    for att in range(60):
        H, ok = [], True
        for i in range(R):
            k = len(A[i])
            if i == R - 1:
                H += [[r.randint(1, P[i][2]) for _ in range(k)]]
                continue
            f = F[i]
            C = [j for j in range(k) if f[j]["c"]]
            S = [j for j in range(k) if f[j]["sq"]]
            E = [j for j in range(k) if not f[j]["c"] and not f[j]["sq"]]
            if len(C) < N[i]: ok = False; break
            lg = set(r.sample(C, N[i]))
            want = ([r.choice(S)] if S else []) + ([r.choice(E)] if E else [])
            if i and r.random() < .5: want.reverse()
            if r.random() < .35: want = want[:1] if i else want[:1] or want
            for j in want:
                if len(lg) < k - 1: lg.add(j)
            for j in range(k):
                if len(lg) < k - 1 and j not in C and r.random() < .2: lg.add(j)
            if i == 0 and S and not (lg & set(S)): ok = False; break
            H += [hang(i, lg)]
        if not ok: continue
        L = [[H[i][j] == P[i][2] for j in range(len(A[i]))] for i in range(R)]
        alive = 0
        for w, f in zip(WT, RIV):
            if all(sum(1 for j in range(len(A[i])) if i < R - 1 and f(F[i][j], L[i][j])) == N[i]
                   for i in range(R)):
                alive += w
        if best is None or alive < best[0]: best = (alive, H)
        if not alive: break
    plain = [hang(i, set([j for j in range(len(A[i])) if F[i][j].get("c")][:N[i]]))
             if i < R - 1 else [P[i][2]] * len(A[i]) for i in range(R)]
    for H in ([best[1]] if best else []) + [plain]:
        s = draw(H)
        if chk(s): return s
    return ""
